AGENDA
  CITY COUNCIL MEETING
  OCTOBER 18, 2022
UNTIL FURTHER NOTICE, MEETINGS WILL BE CONDUCTED PURSUANT TO THE PROVISIONS OF
ASSEMBLY BILL 361, WHICH ALLOWS COUNCIL MEMBERS TO PARTICIPATE FROM A REMOTE
LOCATION WITHOUT LISTING A PHYSICAL LOCATION. TO PROVIDE COMMENTS DURING A MEETING:
YOU MAY ATTEND THE MEETING, SEND AN EMAIL TO: publiccomments@norwalkca.gov, OR JOIN THE
ZOOM MEETING BY CALLING: (669) 900-6833 OR USING THE ZOOM APP WITH THE FOLLOWING LINK:
https://us02web.zoom.us/j/7095732685; MEETING ID: 709 573 2685. THE MEETING MAY BE VIEWED
THROUGH ZOOM, FIOS CHANNEL 32 OR CHARTER CHANNEL 3, OR ON THE CITY'S WEBPAGE AT:
https://www.norwalk.org/city-hall/meeting-agendas-393.
  6:00 PM
  NORWALK CITY HALL/COUNCIL CHAMBERS
  AND VIA VIDEOCONFERENCE

  Rick Ramirez, Mayor
  Ana Valencia, Vice Mayor
  Tony Ayala, Councilmember
  Jennifer Perez, Councilmember
  Margarita L. Rios, Councilmember
  Public Comment: Comments may be made in person, submitted via email at: publiccomments@norwalkca.gov, or through
  the video conference during the designated time on any item on the agenda or on any other matter within the jurisdiction
  subject to the rules of decorum described in Norwalk Municipal Code §2.08.020. The maximum time allowed is three
  minutes.

  Pursuant to provisions of the Brown Act, no action may be taken on a matter unless it is listed on the agenda, or unless
  certain emergency or special circumstances exist. The City Council may direct staff to investigate and/or schedule certain
  matters for consideration at a future City Council meeting.

  Please adhere to the following procedures when addressing the Council:

  • Comments should be limited to 3 minutes or less.
  • Comments should be directed to the City Council as a whole and not directed to individual Councilmembers.

  Americans with Disabilities Act: In compliance with the ADA, if you need special assistance to participate in a City
  meeting or other services offered by this City, please contact the City Clerk's Department, (562) 929-5720. Assisted listening
  devices are available at this meeting. Ask the City Clerk if you desire to use this device. Upon request, the agenda and
  documents in the agenda packet can be made available in appropriate alternative formats to persons with a disability.
  Notification of at least 48 hours prior to the meeting or time when services are needed will assist the City staff in assuring
  that reasonable arrangements can be made to provide accessibility to the meeting or service.

  Note: Any writings and/or documents provided to a majority of the City Council regarding any item on this agenda after it
  has been posted will also be made available for public inspection.

  Writings and/or documents are available for inspection in the City Clerk's Department, City Hall, 12700 Norwalk Boulevard
  during regular business hours, 8:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m., Monday - Thursday and 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., every other Friday;
  telephone (562) 929-5720. You may also contact the City Clerk via e mail at recordsrequests@norwalkca.gov.

  CLOSED SESSION MEETING – 5:00 p.m.
 CALL TO ORDER
  Mayor Ramirez

ROLL CALL
  Theresa Devoy, CMC
  City Clerk

ORAL COMMUNICATIONS FOR CLOSED SESSION MATTERS

CLOSED SESSION

  I.  CONFERENCE WITH LEGAL COUNSEL – ANTICIPATED  LITIGATION  PURSUANT  TO
  GOVERNMENT CODE §54956.9(d)(4) in one case.

  II.  CONFERENCE WITH REAL PROPERTY NEGOTIATOR PURSUANT TO GOVERNMENT CODE
  §54956.8: Assessor Parcel Number 8045-008-902; Negotiating on behalf of the City: Jesus M. Gomez,
  City Manager; Negotiating Party: State of California; Under Negotiation: Price and Terms of Payment.

RECESS

  REGULAR MEETING – 6:00 p.m.

CALL TO ORDER
  Mayor Ramirez

INVOCATION
  Jackeline Vives
  Norwalk United Methodist Church

FLAG SALUTE
  Carmen Mejia
  Lakeland Elementary

ROLL CALL
  Theresa Devoy, CMC
  City Clerk

  CLOSED SESSION REPORT

CITY COUNCIL COMMENTS

  a.  Report of City Council Travel

SPECIAL PRESENTATIONS

  I.  City Council to recognize October 24 - October 28, 2022 as Red Ribbon Week in the City of Norwalk.

  II.  City Council to proclaim October as Down Syndrome Awareness Month in the City of Norwalk.

  III.  City Council to proclaim October as Hindu Heritage Month in the City of Norwalk.

  IV.  City Council to recognize Teen Alliance Program volunteers and Recreation staff for assistance with the
  Social Services Food Pantry Project.

CITY MANAGER COMMENTS

  1.  COVID-19 Update.

  2.  Mercy Housing Groundbreaking recap.
   3.  Mayor’s Inspirational Breakfast recap.

  4.  Paint the Town Pink – Public Service Announcement.

  5.  Halloween Parade recap.

  6.  Bi-Weekly Review.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Consent calendar items are considered routine matters which may be enacted by one motion and roll call vote.
Any item may be removed from the consent calendar and considered separately by City Council.

  1.  WAIVE READING IN FULL OF ALL ORDINANCES ON THE AGENDA - Staff recommends City Council
  waive reading in full of all ordinances on the agenda and declare that said titles which appear on the
  public agenda shall be determined to have been read by title and further reading waived.

  2.  MEETING MINUTES – Staff recommends City Council approve the minutes of the meeting of October
  4, 2022. 825-04

  Minutes

  3.  PAYROLL – Staff recommends City Council approve the payroll for the period September 18, 2022 –
  October 1, 2022, in the total amount of $1,037,316.08. 630

  Report

  4.  COMMERCIAL DEMANDS – Staff recommends City Council approve the warrant register period
  September 27, 2022 – October 10, 2022 in the total amount of $2,102,711.91. 640

  Warrant Register

  5.  CLAIM AGAINST THE CITY – Staff recommends City Council deny the claim filed by Interinsurance
  Exchange Automobile Club. 830-09

  Report

  6.  ASSEMBLY BILL 361 FINDINGS - Staff recommends City Council make the following findings:

  a.  City Council has reconsidered the circumstances of the state of emergency.

  b.  Both of the following circumstances exist (i) The state of emergency continues to directly impact
  the ability of the members to meet safely in person and (ii) City Council continues to impose or
  recommend measures to promote social distancing including remote or hybrid meeting
  participation. 825

  Report

  7.  ORDINANCE NO. 22-1733 - AMENDING CHAPTER 8.60 TO TITLE OF THE NORWALK MUNICIPAL
  CODE PROHIBITING SMOKING IN MULTI-UNIT RENTAL DWELLINGS – Staff recommends City
  Council accept for second reading and adopt Ordinance No. 22-1733, AN ORDINANCE OF THE CITY
  COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF NORWALK ADDING CHAPTER 8.60 TO TITLE 8 OF THE NORWALK
  MUNICIPAL CODE TO PROHIBIT SMOKING IN MULTI-UNIT RENTAL DWELLINGS.

  Report

  8.  ENTERTAINMENT DISTRICT – CIVIC CENTER PLAN / ORDINANCE NO. 22-1734 – ADOPTING
  ZONING TEXT AMENDMENT NO. 2022-01 AND ORDINANCE NO. 22-1735 – APPROVING A
  DEVELOPMENT AGREEMENT – Staff recommends City Council adopt:

  a.  Ordinance No. 22-1734, AN ORDINANCE OF THE CITY OF NORWALK ADOPTING ZONING
  TEXT AMENDMENT NO. 2022-01 ESTABLISHING THE NORWALK ENTERTAINMENT
  DISTRICT – CIVIC CENTER SPECIFIC PLAN;
   b.  Ordinance No. 22-1735, AN ORDINANCE OF THE CITY OF NORWALK APPROVING
  DEVELOPMENT AGREEMENT NO. 2022-01 BY AND BETWEEN THE CITY OF NORWALK AND
  PRIMESTOR DEVELOPMENT, INC.

  Report

  9.  AGREEMENTS – HEALTH ON WHEELS PROGRAM – Staff recommends City Council:

  a.  approve the Health on Wheels agreement with the Norwalk-La Mirada Unified School District and
  California State University Long Beach to provide free and accessible basic health care services to
  children in the Norwalk-La Mirada Unified School District from October 1, 2022 through June 30,
  2023, with two automatic renewal terms of one year each thereafter;

  b.  approve the Bailment agreement with Norwalk-La Mirada Unified School District, for storage of a
  motor home vehicle at the Norwalk City Yard from October 1, 2022 through June 30, 2025; and

  c.  authorize the City Manager to execute the HOW Program and Bailment agreements and any
  amendments provided there is funding in the budget, on behalf of the City, in a forms approved by
  the City Attorney.

  Report

  10. CORONAVIRUS PANDEMIC – OCTOBER EMERGENCY OPERATIONS CENTER UPDATE –
  Receive and file.

  Report

APPOINTMENTS

  11. ADVISORY BODIES – Staff recommends City Council make appointments to fill the vacancies on the
  various City advisory bodies. 200

  Report

ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS

  12. ORDINANCE NO. 22-1736 - ADDING CHAPTER 9.30 “SPEED CONTESTS OR EXHIBITIONS OF
  SPEED” TO TITLE 9 OF THE NORWALK MUNICIPAL CODE - Staff recommends City Council
  introduce by title only, Ordinance No. 22-1736, AN ORDINANCE OF THE CITY OF NORWALK
  ADDING CHAPTER 9.30 “SPEED CONTESTS OR EXHIBITIONS OF SPEED” OF TITLE 9 (“PUBLIC
  PEACE, MORALS AND WELFARE”) OF THE NORWALK MUNICIPAL CODE TO PROHIBIT
  SPECTATORS AT ILLEGAL SPEED CONTESTS OR EXHIBITIONS OF SPEED, and schedule for
  adoption.

  Report

  13. ORDINANCE NO. 22-1737 ADDING CHAPTER 9.31 “UNLAWFUL POSSESSION OF CATALYTIC
  CONVERTERS” OF TITLE 9 (“PUBLIC PEACE, MORALS AND WELFARE”) OF THE NORWALK
  MUNICIPAL CODE TO PROHIBIT THE UNLAWFUL POSSESSION OF CATALYTIC CONVERTERS IN
  THE CITY - Staff recommends City Council introduce by title only Ordinance No. 22-1737, AN
  ORDINANCE OF THE CITY OF NORWALK ADDING CHAPTER 9.31 “UNLAWFUL POSSESSION OF
  CATALYTIC CONVERTERS” TO TITLE 9 OF THE NORWALK MUNICIPAL CODE, and schedule for
  adoption.

  Report

PUBLIC HEARING

  14. RESOLUTION NO. 22-60 – APPLICATION FOR GRANT FUNDING FROM THE CALIFORNIA
  DEPARTMENT OF HOUSING AND COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT’S PERMANENT LOCAL
  HOUSING ALLOCATION PROGRAM - Staff recommends City Council adopt Resolution No. 22-60, A
  RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF NORWALK APPROVING THE
  APPLICATION FOR GRANT FUNDING FROM THE CALIFORNIA DEPARTMENT OF HOUSING AND
   COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT’S PERMANENT LOCAL HOUSING ALLOCATION PROGRAM, AND
  AUTHORIZING THE CITY MANAGER TO EXECUTE ALL RELATED DOCUMENTS.

  Report

ORAL COMMUNICATIONS

ADJOURNMENT

I hereby certify under penalty of perjury under the laws of the State of California that the foregoing agenda was posted
on the City Hall bulletin board not less than 72 hours prior to the meeting. Dated October 13, 2022.

Theresa Devoy, CMC
City Clerk
